messages:
nina: Heads up — our forecasting pipeline is showing a recurring midweek bump in projected GPU hours. Seen this 3 weeks in a row. Dash: https://grafana.redwood/team/infra/d/Fxxgpu/usage-forecast. Spike concentrated in eu-west. Can infra/telemetry folks look?

sam: Do we know if this is a real user-driven demand spike or a telemetry/aggregation artifact?

jia: Quick hypothesis — we changed ingestion sampling for embeddings in eu-west on 2026-02-10 (sampling=0.5) then reverted on 02-18. Could be a coverage shift affecting the model that generates the forecast.

alejandro: I pulled raw usage. The raw GPU_seconds series shows short-duration higher tail on Tue/Wed nights. Looks real but noisy.

sam: Are we comparing the same metric? Forecast uses daily gpu_hours (derived), while many dashboards use summed gpu_seconds. Possible mismatch in aggregation window. Example query I ran:
```sql
SELECT date_trunc('day', event_time) as day, sum(gpu_seconds)/3600 AS gpu_hours
FROM usage_events
WHERE region = 'eu-west' AND event_time >= '2026-01-15'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
```

nina: Good catch. Forecast job config: `aggregation.window = 24h`, `window_alignment = UTC`. Our Grafana panel aggregates by local date (CET) which shifts the apparent spikes.

jia: Also noticed kafka-ingest had a short lag on 2026-02-24 during the largest spike — topic `usage-events-eu` had a transient partition lag ~120s while producers retried. Could have batched a bunch of events that landed same day. Logs: `producer: retry, batch flushed` around 02:10Z.

alejandro: Network note — we saw increased retransmits from eu-west -> s3 gateway that morning. Might explain bursty flushes. tcp_retransmits jumped to 5% for a 10m window.

priya: Proposed action list: 1) normalize aggregation windows between forecast and dashboards (owner: sam) 2) run a targeted backfill for 2026-02-22..2026-02-25 from raw S3 and re-run the forecast model (owner: priya) 3) add a telemetry metric for ingestion-batch-size and kafka-lag heatmap for eu regions (owner: jia) 4) quick cost sensitivity: simulate +10% weekly midweek bump to see committed capacity impact (owner: nina).

sam: I can update the Grafana panels to use UTC-aligned day and add a note. Will also add a one-off panel comparing `gpu_seconds/3600` vs forecast `gpu_hours`. ETA: today EOD.

priya: I'll start the backfill — path is `s3://redwood-telemetry/raw/eu-west/2026-02/` — planning to run mapreduce job that recomputes `gpu_seconds` per 1s buckets then upsample to hourly. Backfill job id: `backfill-20260224-eu-1`.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rebuild-ingest-job #842 deployed to prod at 2026-02-15T03:12Z by sam.

jia: For the new telemetry metric, suggested PromQL: `sum by (region) (rate(kafka_consumer_lag_total{topic="usage-events"}[5m]))` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(kafka_consumer_batch_size_seconds_bucket[5m]))` to capture tails.

alejandro: Cost note — if midweek bump is sustained +10% on GPU-hours, annualized delta is ~+120k USD on current reserved pricing. We should simulate on the committed capacity dashboard before proposing any capacity commits.

nina: Let's treat today as data-fix day + dashboard alignment. If backfill reduces the forecast the on-call can skip increasing Dedicated capacity. Keep communication to customers minimal for now.

priya: Backfill job started (tracking id: backfill-20260224-eu-1). I’ll post results here once complete.

sam: Done — Grafana panels updated and note added. Link: https://grafana.redwood/team/infra/d/Fxxgpu/usage-forecast?view=utc-aligned.

priya: Backfill finished — re-run forecast job started at 2026-02-25T14:02Z. Preliminary: daily gpu_hours down ~6% for affected days after recompute. Full forecast recompute still running.

nina: Thanks — update thread when the recompute finishes and we have the new capacity projection. If it's still >5% bump we'll discuss temporary burst capacity options. :thumbsup:
